pages.title: overview
pages.content:
mer_prefer_stage2: Emotion Preference

MER-Prefer is a newly introduced track. The concept of emotion preference was first proposed in EmoPrefer, which predicts which of two emotion descriptions is preferred by human annotators for a given video. This task plays a crucial role in training reward models capable of understanding human emotions.

We provide two training datasets: EmoPrefer-Data with majority-voted labels and EmoPrefer-Data-V2 with single-annotator labels. For testing, we provide 379 samples with majority-voted labels.

See the baseline paper for more details: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19417

Official website: https://zeroqiaoba.github.io/MER-Challenge/

Submission Format

The result file must be named answer.csv with the following columns:

  • name: sample identifier
  • a1: first emotion description (text)
  • a2: second emotion description (text)
  • preference: the preferred description — must be exactly a1 or a2

Compress answer.csv into answer.zip and submit via Codabench.
pages.content_zh:
# mer_prefer_stage2：情感偏好

MER-Prefer 是一个新引入的赛道。情感偏好的概念首次在 EmoPrefer 中提出，该概念针对给定视频预测人类标注者更倾向于哪个情感描述。该任务在训练能够理解人类情感的奖励模型中起着至关重要的作用。

我们提供两个训练数据集：EmoPrefer-Data（多数投票标签）和 EmoPrefer-Data-V2（单一标注者标签）。对于测试，我们提供 379 个样本，均采用多数投票标签。

有关更多详情，请参阅基准论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19417

官方网站：https://zeroqiaoba.github.io/MER-Challenge/

## 提交格式

结果文件必须命名为 answer.csv，包含以下列：

  • name：样本标识符
  • a1：第一个情感描述（文本）
  • a2：第二个情感描述（文本）
  • preference：首选描述 — 必须恰好是 a1 或 a2

将 answer.csv 压缩为 answer.zip 并通过 Codabench 提交。

pages.title: evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation

In MER-Prefer, we evaluate two-class preference classification using Weighted F1-score (WAF) as the primary metric and Accuracy (ACC) as the secondary metric.

For each sample, the submission must predict whether description a1 or a2 is preferred by human annotators. The prediction is evaluated against the ground truth preference labels.

Only samples whose (name, a1, a2) tuple exists in the ground truth set are evaluated.

See the baseline paper for more details: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19417

Official website: https://zeroqiaoba.github.io/MER-Challenge/
pages.content_zh: # 评估 在MER-Prefer中，我们使用**加权F1分数（WAF）**作为主要评估指标，**准确率（ACC）**作为次要评估指标进行二分类偏好分类评估。 对于每个样本，提交内容必须预测人工标注者更倾向于描述`a1`还是`a2`。该预测与地面真实偏好标签进行比较评估。 仅评估在地面真实集合中存在`(name, a1, a2)`元组的样本。 详见基线论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19417 官方网站：https://zeroqiaoba.github.io/MER-Challenge/

pages.content:
MER-Prefer: Emotion Preference

MER-Prefer is a newly introduced track. The concept of emotion preference was first proposed in EmoPrefer, which predicts which of two emotion descriptions is preferred by human annotators for a given video. This task plays a crucial role in training reward models capable of understanding human emotions.

We provide two training datasets: EmoPrefer-Data with majority-voted labels and EmoPrefer-Data-V2 with single-annotator labels. For testing, we provide 379 samples with majority-voted labels.

See the baseline paper for more details: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19417

Official website: https://zeroqiaoba.github.io/MER-Challenge/

Submission Format

The result file must be named answer.csv with the following columns:

  • name: sample identifier
  • a1: first emotion description (text)
  • a2: second emotion description (text)
  • preference: the preferred description — must be exactly a1 or a2

Compress answer.csv into answer.zip and submit via Codabench.

Important Updates from the Organizing Committee Dear MER2026 Participants and Colleagues, Thank you for your continuous support and active participation in the MER2026 challenge. To ensure fairness, robust evaluation, and transparency, the Organizing Committee is issuing important updates regarding the evaluation protocols, specifically for Track 3, as well as overarching rules on method validity. Please review the following information carefully, as it impacts final rankings and submission guidelines. 1. Track 3 (MER-Prefer) Evaluation Updates & Leaderboard Statement To better assess model robustness, the final ranking for Track 3 will now be determined by the average score of Stage 1 (the current test set) and Stage 2 (a supplementary test set).
  • Stage 2 Release:The Stage 2 test set will be released on July 11, AoE.
  • Submission Limit:Each team is allowed strictly ONE submission for Stage 2. A dedicated submission channel will be provided shortly.
  • Deadline:The final submission deadline remains unchanged at July 13, AoE.

Regarding the Current Leaderboard: In response to the exceptionally high accuracy scores on the current Codabench leaderboard, the committee has initiated a technical verification process of the relevant pipelines. The current results remain valid pending this review. Until a definitive conclusion is reached, there is no evidence of misconduct. We kindly urge all participants to remain objective and refrain from spreading unverified speculation that could harm the reputation of individuals or teams.

Post-Competition Reproducibility: After the competition, the first-place team in Track 3 will be required to publicly release fully reproducible materials (e.g., via GitHub), including code, training/testing scripts, model configurations, and instructions. These materials will be open for community review to ensure absolute transparency.

2. Method Validity and Reproducibility (Applicable to All Tracks) All final submissions must be generated by a learnable, reproducible, and generalizable modeling pipeline.
  • Acceptable Practices:Teams may use reasonable preprocessing methods, priors derived from training samples, or components that aid in learning generalizable structures, provided they are part of a complete and auditable pipeline.
  • Prohibited Shortcuts:Submissions must not rely on non-generalizable, competition-specific shortcuts. This includes using sample identifiers (sample_idis strictly an index, not a semantic feature), file naming conventions, test sample ordering, fixed lookups, manual scaling, constant biases, or rules calibrated repeatedly via leaderboard feedback. If priors or calibration terms from training data are used, teams must clearly explain their role and demonstrate their contribution via ablation studies.
  • Format Compliance:All submissions must strictly adhere to the official starting_kitregarding templates, entry functions, file organization, and output formats.
3. Compliance Audits and Verification The organizing committee will conduct random checks during and after the competition. If a submission displays abnormal performance, highly unusual historical fluctuations, or suggests over-reliance on fixed priors or manual calibrations, the committee will contact the team for proof of reproducibility. To verify your methods, you may be required to provide:
  • Trained model weights and source code.
  • Training/inference scripts and configuration files.
  • Random seeds and preprocessing/inference instructions.
  • Ablation study results.
Failure to prove that a submission originates from a legitimate, reproducible pipeline, or the discovery of prohibited shortcuts, will result in the submission being deemed invalid and excluded from the final rankings.
The committee sincerely apologizes for any confusion these rule clarifications and reviews may cause. We are committed to protecting the legitimate rights of all participants while upholding the integrity of the challenge. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation. Best regards, MER2026 Organizing Committee

16944.title: ImageEval 2026 Task 2 - CRAI-Bench - Cultural Accuracy Evaluation for Arabic Text-to-Image Generation
16944.description: Evaluate whether AI-generated images faithfully represent Qatari and Arab cultural scenes using the CRAI framework.
16944.description_zh:
# 使用CRAI框架评估AI生成图像对卡塔尔和阿拉伯文化场景的真实性表现

## 文化准确性（Cultural Accuracy）
- **服饰表现**：评估传统服装（如阿拜亚、古特拉、阿拉伯头巾）的细节准确性
- **建筑风格**：验证伊斯兰建筑元素（如拱形、穹顶、书法装饰）是否正确呈现
- **宗教仪式**：检查礼拜场景、斋月相关元素的真实性
- **社会场景**：评估家庭聚会、市集、传统活动的文化真实性

## 代表性（Representation）
- **多样性**：确保呈现卡塔尔和阿拉伯世界的多元性，避免单一刻板印象
- **地理差异**：区分不同地区的文化特征（城市、沙漠、海滨）
- **代际表现**：反映传统与现代元素的融合
- **性别与身份**：公平准确地呈现不同群体

## 人工制品与物质文化（Artifacts）
- **传统手工艺**：阿拉伯书法、陶艺、纺织品的准确性
- **日常用品**：咖啡器具、香炉等文化象征物
- **装饰元素**：几何纹样、穆斯林花纹设计的准确性
- **食文化**：传统美食呈现的真实性

## 背景与语境（Context）
- **历史准确性**：时代背景的正确性
- **社会背景**：活动场景的合理性与适切性
- **语言符号**：阿拉伯书写的准确性
- **文化敏感性**：尊重宗教和社会禁忌

pages.title: overview
pages.content:
ImageEval2026 Subtask 2: CRAI-Bench: Cultural Accuracy Evaluation for Arabic Text-to-Image Generation

CRAI-Bench evaluates whether AI-generated images faithfully represent Qatari and Arab cultural scenes. Given a reference image, a caption, and an AI-generated image produced from that caption, participants predict CRAI scores across five cultural accuracy dimensions.

CRAI Formula

CRAI = 0.30 × CEA + 0.20 × CC + 0.20 × CS + 0.20 × CI − 0.10 × HP

Score Interpretation

  • 0.85 – 1.00: Highly accurate
  • 0.70 – 0.84: Mostly accurate
  • 0.50 – 0.69: Moderately accurate
  • 0.30 – 0.49: Weak
  • Below 0.30: Poor or misleading

Contact

imageeval2026@gmail.com
pages.content_zh:
ImageEval2026 子任务2：CRAI-Bench：阿拉伯文本转图像生成的文化准确性评估

CRAI-Bench评估AI生成的图像是否真实代表卡塔尔和阿拉伯文化场景。给定参考图像、标题和从该标题生成的AI生成图像，参与者需预测五个文化准确性维度的CRAI分数。

CRAI公式

CRAI = 0.30 × CEA + 0.20 × CC + 0.20 × CS + 0.20 × CI − 0.10 × HP

分数解释

  • 0.85 – 1.00：高度准确
  • 0.70 – 0.84：基本准确
  • 0.50 – 0.69：中等准确
  • 0.30 – 0.49：较弱
  • 低于0.30：较差或误导性

联系方式

imageeval2026@gmail.com

pages.title: evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation

Primary metric: Spearman correlation between predicted and gold CRAI_composite scores. Higher is better.

Secondary metric: MAE on CRAI_composite. Lower is better. Used as tiebreaker.

Per-dimension scores (CEA, CC, CS, CI, HP) are reported on the leaderboard for diagnostic purposes but do not affect ranking.

Organizer Baselines

SystemSpearmanMAE

Submission Format

⚠️ Important: Submit a zip file only containing predictions.tsv with these tab-separated columns:

id    CRAI_CEA    CRAI_CC    CRAI_CS    CRAI_CI    CRAI_HP    CRAI_composite

Rules:

  • All scores must be floats in [0.0, 1.0]
  • Header row is required
  • All instances must be present

pages.title: overview
pages.content:
The 2nd Workshop on Low-level Vision Frontiers (LoViF) @ ECCV 2026

 

AIGC Image Compression Challenge

 

Important Dates

  • 2026.06.15 — Release of the training data
  • 2026.06.16 — Release of the validation data
  • 2026.06.16 — Validation server online
  • 2026.07.18 — Submission Deadline for Decoder Executable Files (Maximum File Size: 5 GB)
  • 2026.07.18 — Release of the final test data
  • 2026.07.23 — Deadline for test result submission
  • 2026.07.23 — Deadline for factsheet submission
  • 2026.07.25 — Preliminary test results released to participants
  • 2026.07.24 — Challenge paper submission deadline (It is encouraged to submit the challenge paper. We will select one outstanding challenge paper award from challenge papers)
  • 2026.09.xx — LoViF workshop, final results, and award announcement (ECCV 2026)

Challenge Overview

The AIGC Image Compression Challenge is organized as part of the 2nd Workshop on Low-level Vision Frontiers with Generative AI, Preference Optimization and Agentic Systems (LoViF), which will be held in conjunction with ECCV 2026.

AIGC images differ from traditional natural-image benchmarks not only in appearance, but also in what needs to be preserved after compression. In many generated images, users care about prompt-aligned object composition, readable text, poster or UI-like layouts, stylized textures, and synthetic local details that are uncommon in classical photography datasets. Once these regions are compressed aggressively, the visible distortion is often not limited to blur or ringing: text can become unreadable, semantic structure can drift, and generated fine patterns can collapse into unrealistic artifacts.

This challenge therefore focuses on AIGC image compression as a distinct problem setting. The goal is to benchmark coding efficiency, perceptual quality, and semantic preservation on a curated dataset of AI-generated images, and to encourage methods that are robust to text-heavy prompts, dense compositional instructions, and model-dependent visual styles. Participants are welcome to explore both conventional and learning-based codecs, including methods tuned for text fidelity, generative texture reconstruction, and prompt-aligned detail preservation.

Motivation for This Competition

While image compression has advanced rapidly, most public benchmarks still emphasize natural images captured by cameras. That leaves a clear gap for AIGC content, where readable text, synthetic patterns, prompt-consistent structure, and stylized regions can be disproportionately damaged by compression artifacts even when conventional distortion metrics remain acceptable.

The released AIGC-IC benchmark is designed around this gap. It contains 1000 images generated by 10 text-to-image models, with prompts drawn from multiple complementary sources including compositional evaluation, dense prompt following, visual text generation, and long-text rendering. The data span both 1K and 2K resolution tiers and preserve the original generated PNG content and output resolution, so that the benchmark reflects realistic AIGC generation artifacts rather than post-hoc resizing effects.

By introducing this benchmark, the AIGC Image Compression Challenge aims to provide a practical and forward-looking evaluation setting for compression of AI-generated imagery. We hope the challenge will encourage algorithms that generalize across generator families, preserve AIGC-specific semantic details, and better reflect how compression quality is perceived on modern generated visual content.

Top-ranked participants will be awarded and invited to submit a technical report describing their methods and solutions. Selected teams may also be invited to present their results in the associated LoViF workshop activities.

More details are available in the data, submission and evaluation pages.

Awards

The following awards will be provided to the top-performing teams:

  • One First-Class Award (Champion):
  • One Second-Class Award:
  • One Third-Class Award:

Provided Resources

  • Scripts: The organizers will provide standard evaluation scripts to facilitate reproducible scoring and leaderboard reporting.
  • Contact: Please use the forum on the challenge page for technical discussions, or directly contact the challenge organizers by email.

第2届低层级视觉前沿工作坊（LoViF）@ ECCV 2026

 

AIGC图像压缩挑战赛

 

重要日期

  • 2026.06.15 — 训练数据发布
  • 2026.06.16 — 验证数据发布
  • 2026.06.16 — 验证服务器上线
  • 2026.07.18 — 解码器可执行文件提交截止时间（最大文件大小：5 GB）
  • 2026.07.18 — 最终测试数据发布
  • 2026.07.23 — 测试结果提交截止时间
  • 2026.07.23 — 信息表提交截止时间
  • 2026.07.25 — 初步测试结果向参赛者发布
  • 2026.07.24 — 挑战赛论文提交截止时间（鼓励提交挑战赛论文。我们将从挑战赛论文中遴选一篇杰出论文奖）
  • 2026.09.xx — LoViF工作坊、最终结果和奖项宣布（ECCV 2026）

挑战赛概述

AIGC图像压缩挑战赛作为第2届低层级视觉前沿工作坊——生成式AI、偏好优化和代理系统（LoViF）的一部分而组织，将与ECCV 2026同期举行。

AIGC图像不仅在外观上不同于传统自然图像基准，在压缩后需要保留的内容上也有所不同。在许多生成图像中，用户关心的是与提示词一致的对象组成、可读的文字、海报或UI式的布局、风格化的纹理以及古典摄影数据集中不常见的合成局部细节。一旦这些区域被激进压缩，可见的失真往往不仅限于模糊或振铃伪影：文字可能变得难以阅读、语义结构可能偏移、生成的精细图案可能坍塌成不真实的伪影。

因此，本挑战赛关注AIGC图像压缩作为一个独特的问题设置。目标是在精心策划的AI生成图像数据集上对编码效率、感知质量和语义保留进行基准测试，并鼓励对文字繁密提示词、密集组合指令和与模型相关的视觉风格具有鲁棒性的方法。欢迎参赛者探索传统和基于学习的编码器，包括针对文字保真度、生成纹理重建和提示词对齐细节保留调优的方法。

竞赛动机

虽然图像压缩已经取得了快速进展，但大多数公开基准仍然强调由摄像机捕获的自然图像。这为AIGC内容留下了明显的空白，其中可读的文字、合成图案、提示词一致的结构和风格化区域即使在传统失真度量指标仍可接受的情况下也可能被压缩伪影过度损伤。

发布的AIGC-IC基准围绕这一空白而设计。它包含由10个文本到图像模型生成的1000张图像，提示词来自多个互补来源，包括组合式评估、密集提示词追踪、视觉文字生成和长文本渲染。数据涵盖1K和2K分辨率级别，并保留原始生成的PNG内容和输出分辨率，以便基准反映真实的AIGC生成伪影而非事后调整大小的影响。

通过引入此基准，AIGC图像压缩挑战赛旨在为AI生成图像压缩提供一个实用的、前瞻性的评估设置。我们希望该挑战赛能够鼓励在生成器族群间通用、预

pages.content:
The 2nd Workshop on Low-level Vision Frontiers (LoViF) @ ECCV 2026

 

AIGC Image Compression Challenge

 

Data Overview

The official dataset for this challenge is AIGC-IC-1000, a benchmark of AI-generated images curated for image compression research. The release is designed to evaluate coding performance on modern generated content with diverse prompts, model families, and output resolutions. The dataset is composed of:

  • train data: A total of 800 AI-generated images are provided for training. These images are generated by 10 text-to-image models and cover Geneval, DPG-Bench, CVTG-2K, and LongText-Bench style prompts. Additional public datasets are permitted, but all external data sources must be clearly disclosed in the factsheet.
  • validation data: A total of 100 AI-generated images are provided for performance tuning during the Development Phase.
  • test data: A total of 100 AI-generated images are additionally provided for the final evaluation during the Testing Phase.

The full release contains 1000 images in total with an 800/100/100 train/val/test split. Resolution tiers are balanced across roughly 1K and 2K outputs, and the validation and test images preserve the original PNG outputs without resize, crop, or padding.

Data Access

By accessing the data, the participants implicitly agree with the terms and conditions of the challenge.

  • Training Data:
    • Training Dataset (AIGC-IC-1000 train split, 800 PNG images)
  • Development Phase:
    • Validation Data (AIGC-IC-1000 validation split, 100 PNG images)
  • Testing Phase:
    • Test Data: To be released when the Testing Phase begins.

Dataset Characteristics

  • Generation models: 10 text-to-image generators, each contributing 100 images.
  • Prompt sources: 280 samples each from Geneval, DPG-Bench, and CVTG-2K, plus 160 samples from LongText-Bench.
  • Resolution coverage: mixed square, landscape, and portrait outputs at around 1K and 2K resolution tiers.
  • File integrity: released images are PNG files with preserved output resolution and checksum metadata.
References
  1. AIGC-IC benchmark metadata in the accompanying dataset release.
  2. Geneval prompt source.
  3. DPG-Bench prompt source.
  4. CVTG-2K prompt source.
  5. LongText-Bench prompt source.

第2届低层次视觉前沿研讨会（LoViF）@ ECCV 2026

 

AIGC图像压缩挑战赛

 

数据概览

本挑战赛的官方数据集为AIGC-IC-1000，这是一个为图像压缩研究精心策划的人工智能生成图像基准。该发布版本旨在评估现代生成内容的编码性能，涵盖多样化的提示词、模型系列和输出分辨率。数据集组成如下：

  • 训练数据： 共提供800张人工智能生成的图像用于训练。这些图像由10个文本生成图像模型生成，覆盖Geneval、DPG-Bench、CVTG-2K和LongText-Bench风格的提示词。允许使用额外的公开数据集，但所有外部数据源必须在事实说明书中清晰披露。
  • 验证数据： 在开发阶段，提供100张人工智能生成的图像用于性能调优。
  • 测试数据： 在测试阶段，额外提供100张人工智能生成的图像用于最终评估。

完整发布版本包含1000张图像，采用800/100/100的训练/验证/测试分割比例。分辨率层级在1K和2K输出之间大致均衡，验证和测试图像保留原始PNG输出，未经过调整大小、裁剪或填充处理。

数据访问

参赛者在访问数据时，隐含同意挑战赛的条款和条件。

  • 训练数据：
    • 训练数据集 （AIGC-IC-1000训练集，800张PNG图像）
  • 开发阶段：
    • 验证数据 （AIGC-IC-1000验证集，100张PNG图像）
  • 测试阶段：
    • 测试数据： 将在测试阶段开始时发布。

数据集特性

  • 生成模型： 10个文本生成图像模型，每个模型贡献100张图像。
  • 提示词来源： Geneval、DPG-Bench和CVTG-2K各280个样本，加上LongText-Bench的160个样本。
  • 分辨率覆盖： 混合型正方形、横向和纵向输出，分辨率约为1K和2K两个等级。
  • 文件完整性： 发布的图像为PNG文件，保留输出分辨率和校验和元数据。

pages.title: evaluation
pages.content:
The 2nd Workshop on Low-level Vision Frontiers (LoViF) @ ECCV 2026

 

AIGC Image Compression Challenge

 

Development Phase

During the development phase, submissions are evaluated using both fidelity-oriented and perception-oriented metrics under a low-bitrate constraint. The evaluation metrics include PSNR, MS-SSIM, LPIPS, DISTS, and bitrate (BPP). Both PSNR and MS-SSIM are computed in the RGB domain.

This challenge requires participants to submit results at one single bitrate operating point. The average bitrate constraint over the entire dataset is:

average_bpp ≤ 0.025

Submissions violating the bitrate constraint will be considered invalid and will not appear on the leaderboard.

The leaderboard ranking during the development phase will be determined by the following weighted score:

Final_Score = PSNR + 10 × MS_SSIM + 40 × (1 - LPIPS) + 40 × (1 - DISTS)

Test Phase

After the development phase ends, teams intending to participate in the final test phase must submit their decoder executable files together with the corresponding model checkpoints to the challenge organizers. To control model complexity and parameter scale, the total size of the submitted decoder and model checkpoints must not exceed 5 GB. Participants are required to use only the submitted code and corresponding model checkpoints for the final evaluation.

The final ranking will be determined by two perspectives: (i) objective metric measured by final score in objective quality metric; (ii) The subjective metric is assessed by content consistency and perceptual quality measured by human annotations.

Please refer to the Submission page for detailed submission instructions and required file formats.

Final Test Phase - Preliminary Results [TBA]

Preliminary results will be posted here once the evaluation is complete.
pages.content_zh:
# 第2届低级视觉前沿研讨会（LoViF）@ ECCV 2026

# AIGC图像压缩挑战赛

## 开发阶段

在开发阶段，提交物将使用保真度导向和感知导向的度量在低比特率约束下进行评估。评估度量包括PSNR、MS-SSIM、LPIPS、DISTS和比特率（BPP）。PSNR和MS-SSIM均在RGB域中计算。

本挑战赛要求参赛者在**单一比特率操作点**提交结果。整个数据集的平均比特率约束为：

```
average_bpp ≤ 0.02
```

违反比特率约束的提交将被视为无效，不会出现在排行榜上。

开发阶段的排行榜排名由以下加权得分决定：

```
Final_Score = PSNR + 10 × MS_SSIM + 40 × (1 - LPIPS) + 40 × (1 - DISTS)
```

下面提供了度量计算的简化实现。

```python
import sys
import pyiqa

def main(rec_path, gt_path):
    psnr_m = pyiqa.create_metric('psnr')
    ms_m = pyiqa.create_metric('ms_ssim')
    lp_m = pyiqa.create_metric('lpips')
    dists_m = pyiqa.create_metric('dists')

    psnr = float(psnr_m(rec_path, gt_path).detach().cpu().squeeze().item())
    msssim_final = float(ms_m(rec_path, gt_path).detach().cpu().squeeze().item())
    lpips_final = float(lp_m(rec_path, gt_path).detach().cpu().squeeze().item())
    dists_final = float(dists_m(rec_path, gt_path).detach().cpu().squeeze().item())

    final_score = psnr + 10.0 * msssim_final - 20.0 * lpips_final - 25.0 * dists_final + 45.0

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
```

## 测试阶段

开发阶段结束后，打算参加最终测试阶段的团队必须向挑战赛组织者提交解码器可执行文件以及相应的模型检查点。为了控制模型复杂性和参数规模，提交的解码器和模型检查点的总大小不能超过4 GB。**参赛者在最终评估中必须仅使用提交的代码和相应的模型检查点**。

最终排名将由公开度量集合以及组织者的有效性和可重复性验证决定。提交的方法将从重建保真度和感知质量两个角度进行评估，并额外关注AIGC特定的细节，如文本可读性、合成纹理保留和语义一致性。

请参考提交页面以获取详细的提交说明和所需的文件格式。

## 最终测试阶段 - 初步结果[待公布]

评估完成后，初步结果将在此发布。

pages.content:
The 2nd Workshop on Low-level Vision Frontiers (LoViF) @ ECCV 2026

 

AIGC Image Compression Challenge

 

Submission Workflow

The challenge submission process consists of three stages:

  1. Development Phase (due: 2026.07.20): Participants submit a ZIP archive following the required Results Submission Format through the Codabench “My Submissions” page. The evaluation server automatically computes the metrics and updates the public leaderboard.
  2. Code Submission Phase (2026.07.20-2026.07.20): Teams intending to participate in the final test phase must submit their executable/source decoder to the organizers via email. The submitted decoder must be compatible with the bitstreams submitted during the test phase. To limit model size and computational complexity, the size of the submitted executable decoder must not exceed 5 GB.
  3. Final Test Phase (2026.07.20-2026.07.25): Participants must run inference on the released test set using only the corresponding submitted codec, and submit the final ZIP archive via email for evaluation, following the required Results Submission Format.

Results Submission Format ([Submission Example](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BTtGe3wf8GGcg0QvrmNEOD-meaA3ya3w/view?usp=drive_link))

The following submission format must be followed for both the Development Phase and the Final Test Phase submissions.

  1. Please ensure that the reconstructed output images have exactly the same filenames as the corresponding input images (e.g., for an input image named 00001.png, the reconstructed output image must also be named 00001.png). The reconstructed images must preserve the original spatial resolution.
  2. Create a ZIP archive following the structure below: 

    submission.zip
│
├── reconstructed/
│    ├── 000001.png
│    ├── 000002.png
│
├── bitstream/
│    ├── 000001.bin
│    ├── 000002.bin
│
└── readme.txt
    The readme.txt file should contain the runtime per image (in seconds), whether CPU or GPU is used during inference, whether extra training data is used, and a brief description of the submitted method. If your method includes any AIGC-specific tuning, text-preservation heuristics, or model-side priors, document them here. 
    runtime per image [s] : 10.43
CPU[1] / GPU[0] : 1
Extra Data [1] / No Extra Data [0] : 1
Other description: Briefly describe the submitted solution, including dependencies, code links, scripts, training data, or any other relevant information.

Development Phase Submission Guidelines

During the development phase, participants are only required to submit a ZIP archive following the Results Submission Format through the Codabench “My Submissions” page. The evaluation server will automatically compute the metrics and update the public leaderboard. Executable/source decoder are NOT required during the development phase.


Code Submission Phase Guidelines

After the development phase ends, teams intending to participate in the final test phase must submit their executable/source decoder via email to the challenge organizers at: xin.li@ustc.edu.cn

No additional encoder/decoder updates, model retraining, code modifications, or online/test-time fine-tuning are allowed after the Code Submission Phase.

The email subject should follow the format:

[AIGCIC2026] - [AIGC Image Compression] - [YOUR_TEAM_NAME]

The email body must include the following information:

  1. Full challenge name: LoViF 2026 - AIGC Image Compression Challenge
  2. Team name
  3. Team leader’s name and email address
  4. Team name and usernames registered on the LoViF 2026 Codabench server
  5. Attached executable/source decoder, or corresponding download links (Maximum File Size: 4 GB)

The executable/source decoder package must include all trained decoder models and necessary parameters to ensure reproducibility. A README file describing how to run the code is mandatory.


Final Test Phase Submission Guidelines ( The Factsheet template can be found here )

During the final test phase, participants are required to generate and submit a final ZIP archive following the Results Submission Format using only the corresponding submitted codec and pretrained model checkpoints. Final test phase submissions should be emailed to the challenge organizers at: xin.li@ustc.edu.cn

No additional model updates, retraining, or code modifications are allowed after the Code Submission Phase.

The email subject should follow the format:

[AIGCIC2026] - [AIGC Image Compression] - [YOUR_TEAM_NAME]

The email body must include the following information:

  1. Full challenge name: LoViF 2026 - AIGC Image Compression Challenge
  2. Team name
  3. Team leader’s name and email address
  4. Names, email addresses, and affiliations/institutions of all team members
  5. Team name and usernames registered on the LoViF 2026 Codabench server
  6. Attached Factsheet describing training data, compression pipeline, runtime environment, and reproducibility details. Please include both the compiled PDF version and the corresponding source files.
  7. Download links to the FULL final submission ZIP archive following the required Results Submission Format

Top-ranked participants may be invited to contribute to a challenge report summarizing methods and findings from the competition and may be invited to participate in LoViF 2026 workshop dissemination activities.

pages.title: Dataset
pages.content:
# Dataset

ArGuard Task 1 — Track A is built around an Arabic multimodal meme dataset: each instance is an image with overlaid Arabic text (OCR-extracted). Memes are manually annotated for hatefulness.

For **Subtask A1**, every meme has a single binary label from {`Hateful`, `Not Hateful`}.

## Get the data
The official splits live on the Hugging Face Hub at [`QCRI/ArGuard-Task1`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/QCRI/ArGuard-Task1). Download them with the helper script from the starter kit:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/araieval/ArGuard-2026-tasks.git
cd ArGuard-2026-tasks/task1
pip install -r requirements.txt
python data/download_data.py
```

## Splits

| Split        | Records | Labels   | Phase                    | Purpose                                    |
|--------------|--------:|----------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| `train`      |   3,500 | full     | development              | model training                             |
| `dev`        |     500 | full     | development              | hyperparameter selection, local evaluation |
| `dev_test`   |     500 | **none** | development (leaderboard)| submission target for the dev-phase leaderboard |
| `test`       |     500 | full     | final evaluation         | blind ranking (triple-annotated gold)      |

The `dev_test` split is released with labels stripped — that is the file you submit predictions for during the development phase.

## Record schema (after `download_data.py`)
```json
{
    "id": "f9a8…b1.jpg",
    "image_path": "img/f9a8…b1.jpg",
    "text": "OCR-extracted Arabic text…",
    "label": "Hateful" | "Not Hateful" | null,
    "fine_grained_label": ["Mocking", "Incitement"],
    "annotations": []
}
```

## Licence
The dataset is released under **CC BY-NC 4.0** (non-commercial research use only).

## Resources
- Starter kit: <https://github.com/araieval/ArGuard-2026-tasks>
- Task website: <https://araieval.gitlab.io/ArGuard2026/>

16817.title: LifeGenIP Challenge - Unlearnable Videos against Diffusion-based Customization @ ECCV 2026
16817.description: Design protections that perturb video clips so that diffusion-based video customization (I2V and LoRA tuning) fails to reproduce the target identity or follow the attacker prompt.
16817.description_zh:
# 视频防护设计，用于阻止基于扩散的视频定制（I2V和LoRA调优）

## 概述

设计防护机制使扩散模型无法准确再现目标身份或跟随攻击者提示的视频定制方法失效。

## 核心防护策略

### 1. 身份特征扰动
- **面部几何变形**：在视频帧中引入轻微但持续的面部特征偏移
- **皮肤纹理干扰**：添加不可感知的高频纹理噪声，破坏身份特征学习
- **眼睛和嘴部模糊**：针对性地模糊关键生物识别特征

### 2. 时间一致性破坏
- **帧间不一致性注入**：在连续帧中引入微小的视觉变异
- **光流扰动**：改变物体运动模式的潜在表示
- **闪烁伪影**：插入难以察觉的帧间视觉不一致

### 3. 提示跟随阻止
- **语义对抗扰动**：在视频嵌入空间中添加针对常见提示的对抗性噪声
- **属性干扰**：随机改变可被提示引用的视觉属性（颜色、光照、背景）
- **语言-视觉失对齐**：破坏视频内容与文本描述之间的对应关系

### 4. LoRA适应阻止
- **特征空间扰动**：在扩散模型的中间层特征中添加噪声
- **权重梯度噪声**：在LoRA微调期间污染梯度信息
- **秩空间干扰**：扰动低秩更新能够有效操作的特征子空间

### 5. 图像到视频（I2V）防护
- **参考图像扭曲**：对输入参考图像应用几何或光度变换
- **多模态不匹配**：在参考图像和视频序列间创建风格/内容分歧
- **特征提取器欺骗**：针对I2V模型的编码器添加对抗性扰动

## 技术实现方法

### 不可感知扰动
```
- 操作范围：ΔL < 1-2 ΔCIE LAB单位（人眼难以察觉）
- 频率分析：集中在20-60 Hz范围（对视觉系统的屏蔽频率）
- 自适应幅度：根据局部内容复杂度调整扰动强度
```

### 多层防护叠加
- 将多种扰动类型组合应用
- 动态调整干扰参数以对抗自适应攻击
- 在不同视觉处理阶段引入冗余防护

## 评估指标

### 防护有效性
- I2V/LoRA身份再现失败率
- 提示跟随准确度下降
- 攻击成功率相对于未保护视频的减少

### 用户体验保持
- 视频感知质量（VMAF、LPIPS）
- 结构相似性（SSIM）保留率
- 原始内容可识别性

## 防护鲁棒性考虑

- **对抗适应**：防护应抵抗对防护机制的反向工程
- **多模型泛化**：在不同扩散架构上测试防护有效性
- **计算效率**：确保防护处理开销最小化

## 部署场景

- 视频内容保护（防止未授权定制）
- 深伪防御
- 身份隐私保护
- 媒体认证和完整性验证

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# Overview

Official competition page: <https://lifegenip.cc/competition>

🔥 **Phase 1 submission is now open and will remain open until July 15, 2026 (AoE time).**

🔥 **Starting kit of Phase 1 is released on https://github.com/tmllab/ECCV26_LifeGenIP_starting_kit**

👉 **Each team must also submit a [Google form](https://forms.gle/UkgYXdFbPGrSafoP7) for registration. Once we receive your form, we will complete the review within one day, and your team members' Codabench accounts will be approved. If your team needs to update any information, please contact us by email (lifegenip_workshop@googlegroups.com).**

## Background

With recent advances in diffusion-based video generation, anyone can now synthesize high-quality video content from minimal input. This creates serious threats to facial privacy: a malicious attacker can collect publicly available clips of a target person and generate misleading or harmful content about them, from fake news to violations of portrait rights. Protecting video content from such misuse has become a pressing concern.

Current video customization tools follow two paradigms. **Tuning-based methods** fine-tune a video diffusion model (e.g., via LoRA) on a small set of clips of the target person and then generate diverse new videos from text prompts. **Reference-based methods**, such as image-to-video (I2V) models, take a single reference image plus a text prompt and synthesize a clip. Both pathways enable identity misuse. However, video-level protection has received much less attention than image protection. Defenses against tuning-based customization of video diffusion models remain largely unexplored, while existing work mostly targets image-domain editing or reference-based I2V threats.

## Task

Participants design a protection method that perturbs face-centric video clips. Protection succeeds when the customized output either does not reproduce the target identity or does not follow the attacker's text prompt.

## Threat Model

Two attack pathways:

- **Reference-based (I2V).** The attacker samples a single random frame from a protected clip and feeds it together with a text prompt to an I2V model to synthesize a short video. The attack succeeds if the generated video reproduces the target identity and follows the prompt.
- **Tuning-based.** The attacker uses the entire set of protected clips for one identity to fine-tune a video diffusion model via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). The customized model is then prompted to generate new videos. The attack succeeds if the generated videos reproduce the target identity and follow the prompts.

## Evaluation Tracks

- **Effectiveness** measures how strongly the protection breaks customization on the known model. Each protected clip is fed directly into the customization pipeline against the known model.
- **Robustness** measures whether the protection survives attacks that exploit inter-frame relationships. The protected video is first passed through a hidden temporal attack (e.g., temporal averaging) before being used for customization against the known model.
- **Transferability** measures whether the protection generalizes beyond the known model. Submissions are evaluated against hidden video diffusion models.

## Phases and Tracks

**Phase 1 — Preliminary** (open to all registered teams)

- Attack setting: reference-based (I2V).
- Tracks: **Effectiveness** and **Robustness**.

**Phase 2 — Final** (top teams from Phase 1)

- Attack setting: reference-based (I2V) + tuning-based (LoRA).
- Tracks: **Effectiveness**, **Robustness** and **Transferability**.

The final ranking is determined by Phase 2.
pages.content_zh:
# 概览

官方竞赛页面：<https://lifegenip.cc/competition>

🔥 **竞赛将于6月20日开始，启动工具包和报名表将于6月15日发布。**

## 背景

随着基于扩散模型的视频生成技术的最近进展，任何人现在都可以从最少的输入合成高质量的视频内容。这对面部隐私造成了严重威胁：恶意攻击者可以收集目标人物公开可得的视频片段，并生成关于他们的误导性或有害内容，从假新闻到肖像权侵犯。保护视频内容免受此类滥用已成为一个紧迫的问题。

当前的视频定制工具遵循两种范式。**微调方法**在目标人物的小规模视频片段集合上微调视频扩散模型（例如通过LoRA），然后从文本提示生成多样化的新视频。**基于参考的方法**，如图像到视频（I2V）模型，采用单个参考图像加上文本提示来合成视频片段。两种方式都可能导致身份滥用。然而，相比图像保护，视频级别的保护获得的关注要少得多。针对视频扩散模型微调定制的防御手段仍然鲜少被探索，而现有工作主要针对图像域编辑或基于参考的I2V威胁。

## 任务

参赛者设计一种保护方法，对以人脸为中心的视频片段进行扰动。当定制输出要么不能重现目标身份，要么不遵循攻击者的文本提示时，保护成功。

## 威胁模型

两种攻击途径：

- **基于参考的（I2V）。** 攻击者从受保护的视频片段中随机采样单个帧，将其与文本提示一起输入I2V模型来合成短视频。如果生成的视频重现了目标身份且遵循了提示，则攻击成功。
- **基于微调的。** 攻击者使用一个身份的全部受保护视频片段，通过低秩适配（LoRA）来微调视频扩散模型。定制后的模型随后用于生成新视频。如果生成的视频重现了目标身份且遵循了提示，则攻击成功。

## 评估赛道

- **有效性**衡量保护在已知模型上破坏定制的强度。每个受保护的视频片段直接输入到针对已知模型的定制流程中。
- **鲁棒性**衡量保护是否能抵御利用帧间关系的攻击。受保护的视频首先通过隐藏的时间攻击（例如时间平均）处理，然后用于针对已知模型的定制。
- **可转移性**衡量保护是否推广到已知模型之外。提交的方案将针对隐藏的视频扩散模型进行评估。

## 阶段和赛道

**第1阶段 — 初赛**（对所有注册团队开放）

- 攻击设置：基于参考的（I2V）。
- 赛道：**有效性**和**鲁棒性**。

**第2阶段 — 决赛**（来自第1阶段的顶尖团队）

- 攻击设置：基于参考的（I2V）+基于微调的（LoRA）。
- 赛道：**有效性**、**鲁棒性**和**可转移性**。

最终排名由第2阶段决定。

pages.content:
Shared Task on

Identifying misogynistic videos in Dravidian languages

MMLow @ AACL-IJCNLP 2026

The Shared Task on Identifying Misogynistic Videos in Dravidian Languages aims to advance research in multimodal content analysis and online safety by developing automated systems capable of detecting misogynistic content in video data. Misogyny, expressed through hatred, prejudice, discrimination, objectification, or derogatory attitudes toward women, has become increasingly prevalent across social media and video-sharing platforms. Early detection of such harmful content is essential for creating safer and more inclusive digital spaces. In this shared task, participants will be provided with a curated collection of videos in two major Dravidian languages: Malayalam and Tamil. Each video may contain spoken content, visual cues, textual overlays, or a combination of these modalities. The primary objective is to build computational models that can analyze the videos and determine whether they contain misogynistic content or non-misogynistic content. Participants are encouraged to explore multimodal approaches that leverage audio, text, visual, and contextual information for effective classification. The task seeks to foster innovation in natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and multimodal machine learning for low-resource languages. The shared task will provide benchmark datasets, evaluation protocols, and performance metrics to facilitate fair comparison among participating systems. The outcomes of this task are expected to contribute to the development of robust content moderation tools and promote responsible AI solutions for combating online gender-based hate and discrimination in Dravidian language communities.

Objective: Identify videos in Dravidian languages containing misogynistic content

Languages: Malayalam and Tamil

Details: Participants will be provided with videos in Malayalam and Tamil and are required to classify these comments into misogynistic and non-misogynistic. This task requires a deeper level of multimodal understanding and precision.

    • Note: Do not submit your results directly on the Codabench platform.
  • Timeliness: It is crucial to follow the submission deadlines strictly. Late submissions may not be considered for evaluation.

Paper Submission Guidelines

  • Format and Naming Convention:
    • Title Format: The title of the paper should follow this format: TEAM_NAME@MMLow 2026: Title of the paper. For example, XYZ@MMLow 2026: Identifying misogynistic videos in Dravidian languages
    • Authors' Names: Ensure that the authors' names on the paper match those entered in the Google Form during result submission.
  • Length and Content:
    • Document Length: The paper should be a maximum of 4 pages, excluding appendix and citations (references).
    • Paper Template: Paper submissions must use the LaTeX templates.

    • Note: Poster and demo submissions should be no longer than 4 pages (plus an unlimited number of pages for references and ethics/broader impact statements).
  • References and Citations:
    • Citing the Dataset: Make sure to cite the dataset and any overview papers relevant to the competition. BibTeX entries for these citations will be provided below.
  • Additional Points:
    • Innovation and Originality: Submissions that demonstrate innovative approaches and original research will be highly valued.

15830.title: Neural encoding with deep neural networks (v9 - 2026-04-20)
15830.description:
Predict fixation-aligned MEG activity (204 gradiometer channels, 110 ms post-fixation) for a held-out subject, given natural scene images and eye movement metadata from the Active Vision Semantics (AVS) dataset.

Sulewski, P., Amme, C., Hebart, M., König, P., & Kietzmann, T. (2025). Why we linger: Memory encoding, rather than visual processing demand, drives fixation timing on natural scenes-evidence from a large-scale MEG dataset.

Academic use only. The AVS dataset and all derived materials are provided exclusively for academic research and educational purposes within the course "Neural encoding with deep neural networks" (SoSe 2026) at Osnabrück University.
15830.description_zh:
# 翻译

预测注视对齐的脑磁图(MEG)活动(204个梯度计通道,注视后110毫秒),基于自然场景图像和来自主动视觉语义(AVS)数据集的眼动元数据,为一个被保留的受试者。

Sulewski, P., Amme, C., Hebart, M., König, P., & Kietzmann, T. (2025). 我们为什么停留:记忆编码而非视觉处理需求驱动自然场景上的注视时间——来自大规模脑磁图数据集的证据。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# MEG Brain Encoding Challenge

## Goal

Build a model that predicts how the human brain responds to visual scenes during natural free viewing. Specifically, you will predict **fixation-aligned MEG activity** — the pattern of neural responses measured across 204 MEG gradiometer channels at 110 ms after each eye fixation onset.

## Background

The data come from the **Active Vision Semantics (AVS)** dataset, in which participants freely explored natural scene photographs while their eye movements and whole-head MEG were simultaneously recorded.

You are given data from five training subjects (subjects 1–5) and asked to generalise to a **held-out subject (subject 60)**, whose scene-viewing behaviour and associated MEG responses form the evaluation set.

## Task

**Challenge 1 — Snapshot encoding at 110 ms**

Given the fixation metadata (scene ID, gaze coordinates, duration, sequence position, etc.) and the corresponding scene images, predict the vector of 204 MEG gradiometer amplitudes at 110 ms post-fixation onset.

**Submission shape:** `(7750, 204)` — one row per fixation in the development set, 204 channels.

## Timeline

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| April 2026 | Challenge opens |
| July 2026 | Challenge closes |

## Limits

- 5 submissions per day
- 50 submissions total
pages.content_zh:
# MEG脑编码挑战

## 目标

构建一个模型，预测人类大脑对自然自由观看视觉场景的反应。具体地说，您将预测**注视对齐的MEG活动**——在每次眼动注视开始后110毫秒时在204个MEG梯度计通道上测得的神经反应模式。

## 背景

数据来自**主动视觉语义学（AVS）**数据集，其中参与者在同时记录眼动和全脑MEG的情况下自由探索自然场景照片。

您获得来自五名训练受试者（受试者1-5）的数据，并被要求推广到**保留的受试者（受试者60）**，其场景观看行为和相关的MEG反应构成评估集。

## 任务

**挑战1——110毫秒处的快照编码**

给定注视元数据（场景ID、凝视坐标、持续时间、序列位置等）和对应的场景图像，预测注视开始后110毫秒时204个MEG梯度计振幅的向量。

**提交形状：** `(7750, 204)` ——开发集中每次注视一行，204个通道。

## 时间表

| 日期 | 事件 |
|------|------|
| 2026年4月 | 挑战开放 |
| 2026年7月 | 挑战关闭 |

## 限制

- 每天5次提交
- 总共50次提交

pages.title: Data
pages.content:
# Data

## What You Receive

All data are distributed through the course repository. You do **not** upload data to Codabench — only your predictions.

### Training data (subjects 1–5)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `training/meg_110ms.npy` | MEG at 110 ms, shape `(n_fixations, 204)` |
| `training/metadata.csv` | Per-fixation metadata (see columns below) |
| `training/channel_names.txt` | Ordered list of 204 gradiometer channel names |
| `avs_scenes/` | Full scene images (shared across subjects) |

### Development set (subject 60)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `subject60/challenge1_dev/metadata.csv` | 7750 fixations for which you submit predictions |

The ground truth MEG for subject 60 is **withheld** and used only for scoring.

## Metadata Columns

Key columns in `metadata.csv`:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `sceneID` | Integer scene identifier — links to image file |
| `mean_gx`, `mean_gy` | Mean gaze position in screen-centred pixels (origin = centre, y-axis up) |
| `duration` | Fixation duration [ms] |
| `fix_sequence` | Fixation index within the trial (1 = first fixation) |
| `time_in_trial` | Time since trial onset [ms] |
| `subject` | Subject identifier |

## Scene Images

Scene images are JPEGs named `{sceneID:012d}_MEG_size.jpg`, scaled to the presentation resolution (1024 × 768 px). Fixation patches (112 × 112 px, centred on gaze) can be extracted using `megcourselib.data.stim.extract_crop()`.
pages.content_zh:
# 数据

## 您将获得的数据

所有数据通过课程资源库分发。您**不**将数据上传到 Codabench — 仅提交预测结果。

### 训练数据（被试 1–5）

| 文件 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| `training/meg_110ms.npy` | 110 ms 时的脑磁图，形状为 `(n_fixations, 204)` |
| `training/metadata.csv` | 每个注视点的元数据（见下表列名） |
| `training/channel_names.txt` | 204 个梯度计通道名称的有序列表 |
| `avs_scenes/` | 完整场景图像（各被试共用） |

### 开发集（被试 60）

| 文件 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| `subject60/challenge1_dev/metadata.csv` | 7750 个注视点，需要提交预测 |

被试 60 的真实脑磁图数据**被隐藏**，仅用于评分。

## 元数据列

`metadata.csv` 中的关键列：

| 列名 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| `sceneID` | 整数场景标识符 — 链接到图像文件 |
| `mean_gx`, `mean_gy` | 屏幕中心坐标系中的平均凝视位置（像素）（原点 = 中心，y 轴向上） |
| `duration` | 注视点持续时间 [ms] |
| `fix_sequence` | 试次内的注视点索引（1 = 第一个注视点） |
| `time_in_trial` | 试次开始后的时间 [ms] |
| `subject` | 被试标识符 |

## 场景图像

场景图像为 JPEG 格式，命名为 `{sceneID:012d}_MEG_size.jpg`，缩放至呈现分辨率（1024 × 768 像素）。注视点补丁（112 × 112 像素，以凝视点为中心）可使用 `megcourselib.data.stim.extract_crop()` 提取。

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation

## Metric

Submissions are evaluated using **Pearson correlation (r)** between predicted and actual MEG amplitudes, computed **independently for each of the 204 channels** across all 7750 fixations in the development set.

This gives a vector **r** ∈ ℝ^204, from which four leaderboard scores are derived:

| Column | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| **Mean r** *(primary)* | `mean(r)` — average encoding across all channels |
| **Median r** | `median(r)` — robust central tendency |
| **Max r** | `max(r)` — best single-channel encoding |
| **Worst-10 Channels** | `mean(r[argsort(r)[:10]])` — average of the 10 worst channels |

Rankings are determined by **Mean r** (higher is better). All other columns are shown for diagnostic purposes.

## Submission Format

1. Create a NumPy array of predictions with shape `(7750, 204)` and dtype `float64`.
   - Row order must match `subject60/challenge1_dev/metadata.csv` exactly.
   - Column order must match `channel_names.txt` exactly (MEG0001 … MEG0204).

2. Save it as `predictions.npy`:
   ```python
   import numpy as np
   np.save("predictions.npy", pred)   # shape (7750, 204)
   ```

3. Zip it (the file must be at the root of the zip, not in a subfolder):
   ```bash
   zip submission.zip predictions.npy
   ```

4. Upload `submission.zip` via the Submit button.

## Validity Checks

The scoring program rejects submissions that:
- Have the wrong shape (anything other than 7750 × 204)
- Contain NaN or Inf values

Invalid submissions receive a score of 0.0 on all columns.
pages.content_zh:
# 评估

## 指标

提交的作品使用**皮尔逊相关系数（r）**进行评估，该系数在开发集的所有7750个注视点中**独立计算每个204个通道**的预测MEG振幅与实际MEG振幅之间的相关性。

这产生一个向量 **r** ∈ ℝ^204，从中导出四个排行榜分数：

| 列 | 定义 |
|--------|-----------|
| **平均 r** *（主要指标）* | `mean(r)` — 所有通道的平均编码 |
| **中位数 r** | `median(r)` — 稳健的中心趋势 |
| **最大 r** | `max(r)` — 最佳单通道编码 |
| **最差10个通道** | `mean(r[argsort(r)[:10]])` — 最差10个通道的平均值 |

排名由**平均 r** 决定（越高越好）。所有其他列仅用于诊断目的。

## 提交格式

1. 创建一个形状为 `(7750, 204)` 且数据类型为 `float64` 的NumPy数组。
   - 行顺序必须与 `subject60/challenge1_dev/metadata.csv` 完全匹配。
   - 列顺序必须与 `channel_names.txt` 完全匹配（MEG0001 … MEG0204）。

2. 将其保存为 `predictions.npy`：
   ```python
   import numpy as np
   np.save("predictions.npy", pred)   # 形状 (7750, 204)
   ```

3. 压缩它（文件必须在zip的根目录下，不能在子文件夹中）：
   ```bash
   zip submission.zip predictions.npy
   ```

4. 通过提交按钮上传 `submission.zip`。

## 有效性检查

评分程序会拒绝以下提交：
- 形状错误（除7750 × 204外的任何形状）
- 包含NaN或Inf值

无效提交在所有列中得分为0.0。

pages.title: Important Notice
pages.content:
# Update on Task 3 HD/ASD Evaluation

We found an issue in the previous calculation of the last two Task 3 metrics, namely Task 3 HD and Task 3 ASD. The evaluation rule has now been updated.

The updated Task 3 evaluation uses the corrected HD/ASD calculation. This update is intended to make the Task 3 distance metrics more reasonable and fair for all participants.

To ensure fairness, each team now has **10 valid submission attempts**. The platform allows up to **15 total submissions** to account for possible submission errors or failed evaluations. However, the number of valid submissions must not exceed 10.

All new submissions will be evaluated using the updated rule. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and thank you for your understanding.

# Important Notice: Final Test Docker Evaluation

The MVAA 2026 challenge has entered the final hidden-test Docker evaluation stage.

Participants must submit a Docker image reference through this CodaBench portal. Direct upload of prediction masks is **not** used for the official final ranking.

## Required Submission

Each team should submit a `submission.zip` containing a root-level `submission.json` file:

    {
      "image": "registry.example.com/mvaa/team001@sha256:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
      "timeout_seconds": 21600
    }

The Docker image must contain the complete inference environment, including model weights, code, runtime dependencies, and an automatic entrypoint.

## Hidden Test Evaluation

After a descriptor is accepted, a private organizer-side CodaBench worker forwards it to the MVAA GPU runner. The runner pulls the Docker image, runs it on the hidden test inputs, computes official DSC/HD/ASD metrics using the private reference annotations, and returns the scores to this CodaBench leaderboard.

The hidden test images and labels are not released to participants. Labels are never mounted into participant containers.

## Hardware Compatibility

The final evaluation server uses an NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB GPU. Submitted images must be compatible with compute capability `sm_70`.

## Method Paper Submission

The MWM2026 method paper submission deadline has been extended to **July 20, 2026**.

Participants should submit their method papers through the MWM2026 website:

https://mwm2026.github.io/

Please note that submitting a method paper is one of the prerequisite conditions for award eligibility.

## Deadline

The final Docker submission deadline is **August 01, 2026, 23:59 (UTC+8)**.

pages.content:
﻿
# MVAA 2026 Final Test ## Docker-Based Hidden Test Evaluation for Mitral Valve Anatomy Analysis
Mitral valve assessment plays a central role in the diagnosis, treatment planning, and intraoperative guidance of structural heart disease. The MVAA challenge evaluates automated methods for mitral valve anatomy analysis across three imaging modalities: cardiac CT, 3D transesophageal echocardiography (3D TEE), and surgical video frames. This CodaBench portal is dedicated to the **final hidden-test stage**. Participants submit Docker images containing their complete inference pipelines. The organizers then run the submitted images on the hidden test set and compute the official metrics using the private reference annotations. ## Final Test Objective The final test phase evaluates whether submitted algorithms can generalize to unseen data under a standardized computing environment. The evaluation covers: - Task 1: cardiac CT segmentation; - Task 2: 3D TEE multi-class segmentation; - Task 3: surgical video frame segmentation. ## Submission Mode For this stage, participants submit a lightweight `submission.zip` containing only a Docker image reference. The Docker image itself must be hosted in an accessible registry and must include all inference code, model weights, and dependencies. Please read the **Final Docker Submission** page before submitting. ## Resources - Challenge website: https://mwm2026.github.io/mvaa - Baseline code: https://github.com/db0725/MVAA - CodaBench platform: https://www.codabench.org/ - Contact: dbd2002@foxmail.com

pages.title: Final Docker Submission
pages.content:
# Final Docker Submission

This page describes the required Docker submission format for the MVAA 2026 hidden test phase.

During the final test phase, participants do **not** upload prediction masks directly. Instead, each team submits a lightweight `submission.zip` containing a Docker image reference. A private organizer-side CodaBench worker will forward the descriptor to the MVAA GPU runner. The runner pulls the image, runs it on the hidden test set, computes official metrics, and returns the scores to CodaBench.

## 1. What to Submit to CodaBench

Submit a single `submission.zip` file with the following structure:

```text
submission.zip
`-- submission.json
```

The root-level `submission.json` must contain:

```json
{
  "image": "registry.example.com/mvaa/team001:final",
  "timeout_seconds": 21600
}
```

Fields:

- `image`: Docker/OCI image reference containing your inference code, model weights, dependencies, and default entrypoint.
- `timeout_seconds`: Optional runtime limit requested by the participant. The default limit is 21600 seconds (6 hours). The hard maximum is 43200 seconds (12 hours).


Privacy note: the submitted Docker image reference is used only for organizer-side evaluation and is not shown in the public leaderboard or detailed result page. Do not put registry passwords or access tokens in `submission.json`. If your image is hosted in a private registry, please make sure the organizers have pull access before submission.

For reproducibility, a digest-pinned image is recommended:

```json
{
  "image": "registry.example.com/mvaa/team001@sha256:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
}
```


## 2. Reference Baseline Docker Image

The organizers provide a public reference baseline Docker image so participants can inspect the expected Docker-based inference style:

```bash
docker pull db0725/mvaa-baseline-infer:final-20260626
```

This image is provided only as a reference example. Participants may build their own images using any compatible environment, as long as the final image follows the input/output contract described below.

## 3. Docker Image Requirements

Your Docker image must include:

- all inference code;
- all model weights and checkpoints;
- all Python/system dependencies required at runtime;
- a default `ENTRYPOINT` or `CMD` that starts inference automatically.

Your Docker image must **not** require:

- internet access at runtime;
- interactive terminal input;
- downloading extra model weights during evaluation;
- access to hidden labels or organizer-only files.

The submitted image must be a Linux `amd64` Docker/OCI image.

## 4. Organizer Runtime Contract

The organizer runner will execute the submitted image with the following input/output contract. The exact Docker flags may vary by organizer-side infrastructure:

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all \
  --network none \
  --memory 28g \
  --cpus 14 \
  --pids-limit 2048 \
  --shm-size 8g \
  --cap-drop ALL \
  --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  -v /hidden/test_data:/input:ro \
  -v /job/output:/output:rw \
  -v /job/work:/work:rw \
  -e MVAA_INPUT_DIR=/input \
  -e MVAA_OUTPUT_DIR=/output \
  -w /work \
  YOUR_IMAGE
```

Your container must:

- read test inputs from `/input`;
- write predictions to `/output`;
- exit with code `0` on success.

## 5. Expected Output Layout

After inference, `/output` should contain:

```text
/output/
|-- t1_ct/
|   |-- task1_predictions.json
|   |-- case001_pred.nii.gz
|   `-- ...
|-- t2_tee/
|   |-- task2_predictions.json
|   |-- case001_pred.nii.gz
|   `-- ...
`-- t3_vid/
    |-- task3_predictions.json
    |-- REC_xxx/frame001_pred.png
    `-- ...
```

Task 1 prediction JSON:

```json
{
  "cases": [
    {
      "case_id": "case001",
      "segmentation": "case001_pred.nii.gz"
    }
  ]
}
```

Task 2 prediction JSON:

```json
{
  "cases": [
    {
      "case_id": "case001",
      "segmentation": "case001_pred.nii.gz"
    }
  ]
}
```

Task 3 prediction JSON:

```json
{
  "cases": [
    {
      "case_id": "REC_xxx_000001",
      "segmentation": "REC_xxx/REC_xxx_000001_pred.png"
    }
  ]
}
```

The `segmentation` field must be a relative path under the corresponding task output folder. Absolute paths and path traversal such as `../` are not allowed.

## 6. Mask Format

Task 1:

- File format: `.nii.gz`
- Labels: `0` for background, `1` for target foreground.

Task 2:

- File format: `.nii.gz`
- Labels: `0` for background, `1` and `2` for the two target classes.

Task 3:

- Recommended file format: `.png`
- Labels: `0` for background, any positive value for foreground. Binary masks using `255` for foreground are recommended.

## 7. GPU Compatibility

The official final-test server uses:

```text
GPU: NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB
CUDA driver: 550.x / CUDA 12.4
Compute capability: sm_70
```

Your Docker image must be compatible with NVIDIA V100 / `sm_70`. Do not rely on Ampere/Ada/Hopper-only features such as BF16-only execution, TF32-only kernels, or CUDA extensions compiled only for `sm80`, `sm86`, or `sm89`.

If you compile custom CUDA extensions, include:

```bash
TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.0"
```

## 8. Minimal Dockerfile Example

```dockerfile
FROM pytorch/pytorch:2.5.1-cuda12.4-cudnn9-runtime

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
ENV MVAA_INPUT_DIR=/input
ENV MVAA_OUTPUT_DIR=/output

WORKDIR /workspace

COPY requirements.txt /workspace/requirements.txt
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /workspace/requirements.txt

COPY src/ /workspace/src/
COPY weights/ /workspace/weights/
COPY run.sh /workspace/run.sh
RUN chmod +x /workspace/run.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/workspace/run.sh"]
```

Example `run.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

INPUT_DIR="${MVAA_INPUT_DIR:-/input}"
OUTPUT_DIR="${MVAA_OUTPUT_DIR:-/output}"

mkdir -p "${OUTPUT_DIR}/t1_ct" "${OUTPUT_DIR}/t2_tee" "${OUTPUT_DIR}/t3_vid"

python /workspace/src/infer.py \
  --input "${INPUT_DIR}" \
  --output "${OUTPUT_DIR}"
```

## 9. Local Test Command

Before final submission, test your image locally:

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all \
  --network none \
  -v /path/to/test_input:/input:ro \
  -v /path/to/output:/output:rw \
  your-image:final
```

Then package `submission.json`:

```bash
zip submission.zip submission.json
```

# 最终Docker提交

本页面描述了MVAA 2026隐藏测试阶段所需的Docker提交格式。

在最终测试阶段，参赛者**不**直接上传预测掩模。相反，每个团队需要提交一个包含Docker镜像引用的轻量级`submission.zip`。私有的组织方CodaBench工作程序将描述符转发给MVAA GPU运行器。运行器拉取镜像，在隐藏测试集上运行，计算官方指标，并将分数返回给CodaBench。

## 1. 提交到CodaBench的内容

向CodaBench提交单个`submission.zip`文件，结构如下：

```text
submission.zip
`-- submission.json
```

根级`submission.json`必须包含：

```json
{
  "image": "registry.example.com/mvaa/team001:final",
  "timeout_seconds": 21600
}
```

字段说明：

- `image`：Docker/OCI镜像引用，包含您的推理代码、模型权重、依赖项和默认入口点。
- `timeout_seconds`：可选的参赛者请求的运行时限制。默认限制为21600秒（6小时）。硬性最大值为43200秒（12小时）。

隐私提示：提交的Docker镜像引用仅用于组织方端的评估，不会在公共排行榜或详细结果页面中显示。不要在`submission.json`中放置镜像仓库密码或访问令牌。如果您的镜像托管在私有仓库中，请确保在提交前组织方有拉取权限。

为了确保可重复性，建议使用摘要固定的镜像：

```json
{
  "image": "registry.example.com/mvaa/team001@sha256:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

- 运行时网络访问；
- 交互式终端输入；
- 评估过程中下载额外的模型权重；
- 访问隐藏标签或仅组织方可访问的文件。

提交的镜像必须是Linux `amd64` Docker/OCI镜像。

### Option 2: Google Drive

Both links are required for the complete released dataset:

- Link 1: https://drive.google.com/file/d/14WneBUBZ1X4p69tRdRzximNb0IsWuh2B/view?usp=sharing
- Link 2: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1K4vFo-4pdL1_xt-8msO-32bc2aEdJ7wS/view?usp=sharing

## Hidden Test Data

The hidden test set is not distributed to participants. During final evaluation, the organizers mount the hidden test inputs into each submitted Docker container at:

```text
/input
```

The hidden test labels are only accessible to the organizer-side scorer and are never mounted into participant containers.

## Baseline Code and Reference Docker Image

Participants can access the official baseline and documentation here:

- https://github.com/db0725/MVAA

The baseline is intended as a reference implementation. A public reference Docker image is also available for participants who want to inspect the expected Docker-based inference style:

```bash
docker pull db0725/mvaa-baseline-infer:final-20260626
```

Final submissions must follow the Docker format described in the **Final Docker Submission** page.

## Task 3 Training Annotation Note

One Task 3 video training sample may contain an annotation issue:

```text
t3_vid/train/REC_20250322_101917_746A/REC_20250322_101917_746A_000130.png
```

Participants may choose to exclude this sample during model training or data cleaning. This issue is limited to the listed training sample; the validation and hidden test annotations are not affected.

pages.title: Core Task
pages.content:
# Core Task

The MVAA challenge is designed to reflect the real-world clinical workflow across multiple imaging modalities. The challenge is structured into three primary segmentation tasks.

### Participation and Model Submission Requirements

Participants are required to complete and submit results for all three tasks. The official final ranking will be determined using the normalized final score described on the **Final Ranking** page; therefore, submissions for only one or two tasks will not be sufficient for the final ranking.

However, participants are not required to use a single unified multimodal model. Each task may be addressed independently, and participants may train and submit separate models for the CT, 3D TEE, and surgical video frame segmentation tasks.

### Task 1: Mitral Valve Segmentation in Cardiac CT
This task focuses on the automated, multi-class anatomical segmentation of the mitral valve from 3D cardiac CT scans.
*   **Target:** Participants are required to segment the mitral annulus and the anterior/posterior leaflets.
*   **Clinical Significance:** High-resolution CT segmentation provides the precise spatial geometry necessary for pre-procedural planning, including device sizing and the selection of repair strategies for interventions like TEER or annuloplasty.

### Task 2: Mitral Valve Segmentation in 3D Transesophageal Echocardiography (3D TEE)
This task addresses the segmentation of valve structures from volumetric 3D TEE (ultrasound) data, which serves as the key intraoperative reference for valve function.
*   **Target:** Delineation of the valve leaflets from 3D ultrasound volumes.
*   **Technical Focus:** Algorithms must be robust enough to handle ultrasound-specific artifacts, acoustic noise, signal dropout, and ambiguous boundaries between the leaflets and surrounding cardiac tissues.

### Task 3: Mitral Valve Segmentation from Surgical Video Frames
This task focuses on extracting anatomical information from individual frames extracted from intraoperative surgical videos.
*   **Target:** Pixel-level segmentation of the mitral valve structures as seen from the surgeon's direct viewpoint.
*   **Methodology:** Although the data originates from video recordings, this task is defined as a frame-based segmentation problem. Participants should treat the provided frames as individual 2D images for training and inference.
*   **Clinical Focus:** This task enables the verification of leaflet motion and structural continuity during the actual intervention, providing real-time feedback within the surgical environment.
pages.content_zh:
# 核心任务

MVAA挑战赛旨在反映多个成像模态下的真实临床工作流程。该挑战赛结构包含三个主要分割任务。

### 参赛和模型提交要求

参赛者需要完成并提交全部三个任务的结果。官方最终排名将根据**最终排名**页面中描述的归一化最终得分确定；因此，仅提交一个或两个任务的结果将不足以获得最终排名。

但是，参赛者不需要使用单一的统一多模态模型。每个任务可以独立处理，参赛者可以为CT、3D TEE和手术视频帧分割任务分别训练和提交不同的模型。

### 任务1：心脏CT中的二尖瓣分割
该任务重点关注从三维心脏CT扫描中进行二尖瓣多类解剖结构的自动分割。
*   **目标：** 参赛者需要分割二尖瓣环以及前/后瓣叶。
*   **临床意义：** 高分辨率CT分割提供了精确的空间几何信息，用于术前规划，包括器械尺寸确定和修复策略选择，适用于TEER或瓣环成形术等介入治疗。

### 任务2：三维经食管超声心动图(3D TEE)中的二尖瓣分割
该任务涉及从容积3D TEE(超声)数据中进行瓣膜结构分割，其作为瓣膜功能的关键术中参考。
*   **目标：** 从3D超声容积数据中描绘瓣叶轮廓。
*   **技术重点：** 算法必须足够稳健以处理超声特有的伪影、声学噪声、信号丢失以及瓣叶与周围心脏组织间的模糊边界。

### 任务3：手术视频帧中的二尖瓣分割
该任务重点关注从术中手术视频中提取的单个帧中提取解剖学信息。
*   **目标：** 从外科医生直接视角看到的二尖瓣结构进行像素级分割。
*   **方法学：** 虽然数据源自视频记录，但该任务被定义为基于帧的分割问题。参赛者应将提供的帧作为单个2D图像进行训练和推理。
*   **临床重点：** 该任务能够在实际介入治疗中验证瓣叶运动和结构连续性，在手术环境中提供实时反馈。

pages.title: Dataset
pages.content:
# MVAA Challenge - Dataset System

## 1. Ethics Approval & Data License

### 1.1 Ethics Approval
All data is anonymized, with approval from the Medical Ethics Committee (No. KY-N-2022-048-01).

### 1.2 Data Usage Agreement & License
* **License:** CC BY-NC (Attribution-NonCommercial)
* No commercial use of the data is permitted; all usage must comply with the license terms.

## 2. Data Source

### 2.1 Acquisition Devices
* **Cardiac CT:** Siemens Healthineers, GE Healthcare, Philips Healthcare, and Canon Medical Systems.
* **3D TEE:** Philips Epiq cardiac ultrasound system.
* **Surgical Video:** Standard endoscopic video recorder (720p, 30fps).

### 2.2 Acquisition Centers
The dataset is collected from multiple clinical centers, including:
* Guangdong Provincial People’s Hospital
* The First Affiliated Hospital of Jinan University
* Dongguan Eastern Central Hospital

## 3. Dataset Scale & Partition

### 3.1 Task 1: Cardiac CT Segmentation
* **Training Set:** 1,067 images total (27 with ground-truth labels, 1,040 unlabeled for semi-supervised learning).
* **Validation Set:** 30 images (without labels).

### 3.2 Task 2: 3D TEE Segmentation
* **Training Set:** 105 images with ground-truth labels.
* **Validation Set:** 20 images (without labels).

### 3.3 Task 3: Surgical Frame Segmentation

* **Training Set:** 1,559 frames total.
    * **Labeled Data:** 180 frames (118 frames contain the mitral valve).
    * **Unlabeled Data:** 1,379 frames (for semi-supervised learning).
* **Validation Set:** 48 images (without labels, all containing mitral valve structures for scoring).

#### 3.3.1 Task 3 Label Note

Task 3 labels may include annotations beyond the mitral valve. Only the mitral valve label is used for training and evaluation. In this task, the mitral valve is the only target segmentation class.

Participants should use the `*_Label.nii.gz` file within each `*_Label.tar` archive as the source of ground-truth annotations, and refer to the category mapping table in the corresponding `*_Label.json` file for confirmation. Specifically, category ID `10` corresponds to the mitral valve.

The `*_Label.json` file is intended only for reading category names, colors, and metadata, and should not be used as the primary label source for training.

Some polygon annotations in the JSON files are incomplete or empty; therefore, generating training labels from `Polys.Shapes` is not recommended. Of the 180 labeled frames, 118 contain valid mitral valve annotations. Unlabeled frames may also include images without visible mitral valve structures.


## 4. Data Novelty
* **Multi-modal Data Resource:** The challenge includes cardiac CT, 3D TEE, and surgical video data collected from multiple clinical centers. In the current public release, these modalities are provided as independent datasets, and no formal CT-video pairing metadata or case mapping table is included.
* **Unpublished Data:** More than 140 newly collected, unpublished ultrasound images have been provided for validation and testing to ensure fair evaluation of generalization.

## 5. Inclusion & Exclusion Criteria

### 5.1 Inclusion Criteria
1. Standard clinical cardiac views suitable for mitral valve assessment.
2. Sufficient image quality for expert annotation of leaflets and annulus.
3. Availability of corresponding clinical measurement references.

### 5.2 Exclusion Criteria
1. Severe imaging artifacts or signal dropout hindering anatomical visibility.
2. Duplicated or corrupted data.
3. Cases with uncertain clinical reference measurements.

## 6. Annotation Characteristics

### 6.1 Annotation Method
* **Two-Stage Process:** Initial annotations by two trained medical experts followed by review and refinement by a board-certified radiologist with over 10 years of experience.
* **Semi-automated refinement:** For ultrasound data, an initial automatic segmentation was followed by manual review and modification by two annotators until agreement was reached.

### 6.2 Annotation Quality Control (QC)
* **Inter-observer Reliability:** Evaluated on a subset of 30 images using ICC and absolute error distributions.
* **Adjudication:** Senior clinical specialists resolved discrepancies to ensure the reliability of reference annotations.

## 7. Data Preprocessing
1. **Anonymization:** Removal of all patient-related information from metadata.
2. **Standardization:** CT and TEE data converted to NIfTI format; surgical video frames extracted as 2D images.
3. **Resampling:** Data resampled to a consistent resolution to ensure uniform slice-level annotation.

## 8. Main Annotation Error Sources
1. **Inter-Annotator Variability:** Differences in identifying subtle mitral valve boundaries in low-contrast cases.
2. **Annotation Ambiguity:** Inherent ambiguity of valve boundaries due to pathological alterations or imaging limitations.
3. **Technical Limitations:** Errors introduced by the resolution constraints of the annotation tools.

# MVAA挑战赛 - 数据集系统

## 1. 伦理审批与数据许可

### 1.1 伦理审批
所有数据已匿名处理，获得医学伦理委员会批准（编号：KY-N-2022-048-01）。

### 1.2 数据使用协议与许可证
* **许可证：** CC BY-NC（署名-非商业性使用）
* 禁止对数据进行商业使用；所有使用必须符合许可证条款。

## 2. 数据来源

### 2.1 采集设备
* **心脏CT：** 西门子医疗、通用电气医疗、飞利浦医疗和佳能医疗系统。
* **3D TEE：** 飞利浦Epiq心脏超声系统。
* **手术视频：** 标准内窥镜视频录制器（720p，30fps）。

### 2.2 采集中心
数据集来自多个临床中心，包括：
* 广东省人民医院
* 暨南大学第一附属医院
* 东莞东部中央医院

## 3. 数据集规模与划分

### 3.1 任务1：心脏CT分割
* **训练集：** 共1,067张图像（27张带有标注标签，1,040张用于半监督学习的未标注数据）。
* **验证集：** 30张图像（无标签）。

### 3.2 任务2：3D TEE分割
* **训练集：** 105张带有标注标签的图像。
* **验证集：** 20张图像（无标签）。

### 3.3 任务3：手术帧分割

* **训练集：** 共1,559帧。
    * **标注数据：** 180帧（其中118帧包含二尖瓣）。
    * **未标注数据：** 1,379帧（用于半监督学习）。
* **验证集：** 48张图像（无标签，全部包含二尖瓣结构用于评分）。

#### 3.3.1 任务3标签说明

任务3标签可能包含二尖瓣之外的注释。仅二尖瓣标签用于训练和评估。在该任务中，二尖瓣是唯一的目标分割类别。

参与者应使用每个`*_Label.tar`压缩包内的`*_Label.nii.gz`文件作为真值注释的来源，并参考相应`*_Label.json`文件中的类别映射表进行确认。具体而言，类别ID `10` 对应二尖瓣。

`*_Label.json`文件仅供读取类别名称、颜色和元数据使用，不应作为训练标签的主要来源。

JSON文件中的某些多边形注释可能不完整或为空；因此不建议从`Polys.Shapes`生成训练标签。在180个标注帧中，118个包含有效的二尖瓣注释。未标注帧也可能包含不含可见二尖瓣结构的图像。

## 4. 数据新颖性
* **多模态数据资源：** 挑战赛包括来自多个临床中心的心脏CT、3D TEE和手术视频数据。在当前公开发布版本中，这些模态作为独立数据集提供，不包含正式的CT-视频配对元数据或病例映射表。
* **未发表数据：** 提供了超过140张新采集的未发表超声图像用于验证和测试，以确保泛化能力的公平评估。

## 5. 纳入与排除标准

### 5.1 纳入标准
1. 适合二尖瓣评估的标准临床心脏图像。
2. 图像质量足以进行专家标注瓣叶和瓣环。
3. 有相应的临床测量参考数据。

### 5.2 排除标准
1. 严重影像伪影或信号丧失，影响解剖结构的可见性。
2. 重复或损坏的数据。
3. 临床参考测量不确定的病例。

## 6. 注释特征

### 6.1 注释方法
* **两阶段流程：** 先由两名训练有素的医学专家进行初始注释，随后由具有10年以上经验的认证放射学医生进行审核和改进。
* **半自动化精化：** 对于超声数据，初始自动分割后由两名注释者进行手工审核和修改，直至达成一致。

### 6.2 注释质量控制

pages.content:
# Evaluation

## Final Test Evaluation Mode

In the final hidden-test phase, participants submit Docker image descriptors through CodaBench. A private organizer-side CodaBench worker forwards accepted descriptors to the MVAA GPU runner, which pulls each submitted image, runs inference on the hidden test set, computes official metrics, and returns the resulting scores to the CodaBench leaderboard.

Metrics are computed outside the public CodaBench environment on the organizer-side server. The leaderboard columns in this portal are the official hidden-test raw metrics returned by that runner. The official overall ranking is based on normalized metric scores as described on the **Final Ranking** page.

## Metrics

All tasks are evaluated using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff Distance (HD), and Average Surface Distance (ASD). Higher DSC is better; lower HD and ASD are better.

### Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)

DSC measures overlap between the predicted segmentation and the ground truth. It is computed as twice the intersection divided by the sum of the predicted and reference foreground sizes.

### Hausdorff Distance (HD)

HD measures the largest bidirectional surface discrepancy between the prediction and reference mask. Surfaces are extracted from binary masks and Euclidean distances are computed using image spacing when spacing metadata is available.

### Average Surface Distance (ASD)

ASD is the symmetric mean surface-to-surface distance between prediction and reference masks.

## Task-Specific Computation

### Task 1: CT Segmentation

- Foreground label: `1`
- Per-case metrics: DSC, HD, ASD on the binary foreground mask
- Final task score: mean across all Task 1 cases

### Task 2: TEE Segmentation

- Foreground labels: `1` and `2`
- Metrics are computed separately for each foreground class and averaged within each case
- Final task score: mean across all Task 2 cases

### Task 3: Video/Image Segmentation

- Prediction foreground: any positive pixel value
- Reference foreground: the case-specific `target_label`
- Final task score: mean across all Task 3 frames/cases

## Evaluation Notes

- HD and ASD use physical spacing when available; otherwise unit spacing is used.
- Missing or invalid predictions receive penalty metrics: `DSC = 0`, `HD = large penalty`, `ASD = large penalty`.
- If both prediction and reference are empty for an evaluated class, that class is treated as a perfect match: `DSC = 1`, `HD = 0`, `ASD = 0`.
- Prediction paths in JSON files must be relative paths under the corresponding task output folder. Absolute paths and `../` traversal are rejected.

## Leaderboard Columns

The final leaderboard reports:

- `Task1_DSC`, `Task1_HD`, `Task1_ASD`
- `Task2_DSC`, `Task2_HD`, `Task2_ASD`
- `Task3_DSC`, `Task3_HD`, `Task3_ASD`
- `Evaluation_Status`
- `Runtime_Seconds`

`Evaluation_Status = 1` means the organizer-side runner completed successfully. `Evaluation_Status = 0` means descriptor validation, image pulling, inference, or scoring failed; failed submissions receive penalty metrics.

## Participant Result Summary

After a successful final-test submission, participants will see the leaderboard values for the three mean metrics of each task. Per-case or per-image scores are not shown in the final hidden-test phase.

The detailed result summary follows this structure:

```text
MVAA Final Hidden-Test Evaluation
Status: done
Message: official hidden-test evaluation completed

Task-level mean metrics:
- Task 1 (CT): mean DSC = ..., mean HD = ..., mean ASD = ...
- Task 2 (TEE): mean DSC = ..., mean HD = ..., mean ASD = ...
- Task 3 (Video/Image): mean DSC = ..., mean HD = ..., mean ASD = ...

Evaluation_Status: 1
Runtime_Seconds: ...
```

# 评估

## 最终测试评估模式

在最终隐藏测试阶段，参与者通过CodaBench提交Docker镜像描述符。组织方CodaBench工作线程将接受的描述符转发给MVAA GPU运行器，该运行器拉取每个提交的镜像，在隐藏测试集上运行推理，计算官方指标，并将结果得分返回给CodaBench排行榜。

指标在组织方服务器上的公共CodaBench环境外进行计算。此门户中排行榜列显示由该运行器返回的官方隐藏测试原始指标。官方总体排名基于**最终排名**页面中描述的标准化指标得分。

## 指标

所有任务使用骰子相似系数（DSC）、豪斯多夫距离（HD）和平均表面距离（ASD）进行评估。DSC越高越好；HD和ASD越低越好。

### 骰子相似系数（DSC）

DSC测量预测分割与真实标注之间的重叠程度。计算方式为交集的两倍除以预测和参考前景大小之和。

### 豪斯多夫距离（HD）

HD测量预测和参考掩模之间最大的双向表面偏差。表面从二值掩模中提取，当有间距元数据时使用图像间距计算欧几里得距离。

### 平均表面距离（ASD）

ASD是预测和参考掩模之间对称的表面间平均距离。

## 任务特定计算

### 任务1：CT分割

- 前景标签：`1`
- 按病例指标：二值前景掩模上的DSC、HD、ASD
- 最终任务得分：所有任务1病例的均值

### 任务2：TEE分割

- 前景标签：`1`和`2`
- 为每个前景类分别计算指标，在每个病例内进行平均
- 最终任务得分：所有任务2病例的均值

### 任务3：视频/图像分割

- 预测前景：任何正像素值
- 参考前景：病例特定的`target_label`
- 最终任务得分：所有任务3帧/病例的均值

## 评估说明

- 当可用时，HD和ASD使用物理间距；否则使用单位间距。
- 缺失或无效预测收到惩罚指标：`DSC = 0`、`HD = 大惩罚值`、`ASD = 大惩罚值`。
- 如果评估的某个类的预测和参考都为空，该类被视为完美匹配：`DSC = 1`、`HD = 0`、`ASD = 0`。
- JSON文件中的预测路径必须是对应任务输出文件夹下的相对路径。绝对路径和`../`遍历会被拒绝。

## 排行榜列

最终排行榜报告：

- `Task1_DSC`、`Task1_HD`、`Task1_ASD`
- `Task2_DSC`、`Task2_HD`、`Task2_ASD`
- `Task3_DSC`、`Task3_HD`、`Task3_ASD`
- `Evaluation_Status`
- `Runtime_Seconds`

`Evaluation_Status = 1`表示组织方运行器成功完成。`Evaluation_Status = 0`表示描述符验证、镜像拉取、推理或评分失败；失败的提交将收到惩罚指标。

## 参与者结果摘要

成功完成最终测试提交后，参与者将看到每个任务三个平均指标的排行榜值。在最终隐藏测试阶段不显示按病例或按图像的得分。

详细结果摘要遵循以下结构：

```text
MVAA最终隐藏测试评估
状态：完成
信息：官方隐藏测试评估已完成

任务级平均指标：
- 任务1（CT）：平均DSC = ...、平均HD = ...、平均ASD = ...
- 任务2（TEE）：平均DSC = ...、平均HD = ...、平均ASD = ...
- 任务3（视频/图像）：平均DSC = ...、平均HD = ...、平均ASD = ...

Evaluation_Status：1
Runtime_Seconds：...
```

# Final Score, Prizes, and Certificates


The official overall ranking will be based on normalized metric scores from the final hidden-test evaluation. The raw leaderboard metrics will remain visible for transparency, while the normalized score will be used for final ranking and award decisions.

Because Task 2 uses a public dataset, its three normalized metric scores will be assigned as 100 points for all eligible teams to avoid unfair advantage from public test-set information.

To be eligible for prize money, a team must satisfy the participation rules, rank in the overall top 10, and, barring exceptional circumstances approved by the organizers, must attend the onsite presentation.

In addition to the overall awards, the top three teams in Task 1 and the top three teams in Task 3 will receive additional task-specific certificates.

由于第2任务使用公开数据集，其三个标准化指标得分将为所有符合条件的团队分配100分，以避免公开测试集信息带来的不公平优势。

要获得奖金资格，团队必须满足参赛规则、总体排名前10，以及除组织者批准的特殊情况外，必须参加现场展示。
